correctness.rationale: All eight leader-pair orbits are exhausted by the two-hub, hub–leaf, and leaf–leaf cases; exact Schur inverses give spectra; weak majorization and Jensen prove strict dominance for all r>=1; strict trace monotonicity/convexity give unique order thresholds; first two boundaries and asymptotic are derived analytically. The standalone checker performed 1,290 exact-pair inversions and 1,280 independent numerical order comparisons, supplemental only. No unsupported normalization or unproved finite-to-infinite inference.

value.rationale: Perfect-leader placement on two-community trees is a natural fixed-budget decision. The theorem classifies all two-leader choices over an infinite heterogeneous family and continuous objective order, establishes an exact nonempty interval where two standard performance criteria choose disjoint optimal types, and derives a nontrivial linear high-order transition law. These are decision-theoretically and mathematically motivated facts beyond the known first-moment classification.
